old.name: Collobrieres
old.hook: A stone village on a chestnut-shaded river deep inside the Maures, ringed by roughly 2,000 hectares of chestnut groves; the trailhead for the best Maures walks (up to La Verne, up to Notre-Dame-des-Anges) and the self-declared capital of the chestnut.
old.text: A stone village on a chestnut-shaded river deep inside the Maures, ringed by roughly 2,000 hectares of chestnut groves; the trailhead for the best Maures walks (up to La Verne, up to Notre-Dame-des-Anges) and the self-declared capital of the chestnut. The sweet chestnut is the Maures' terroir tree, and the Confiserie Azureenne has candied its marrons in the village for over half a century, roughly seven days steeping in vanilla-scented syrup to make a single marron glace, while the village throws its chestnut festival across three Sundays each October. One real thing to carry away: the marron is a selected large-fruited variety of the wild chataigne, not a separate nut. Signal Chestnut festival held three Sundays each October; Confiserie Azureenne candying marrons here 50-plus years.
